Priya — a couple of immediate thoughts ahead of the workshop:

1) Split-horizon DNS is the least friction if you control the VPC DNS (Route53 private hosted zone or cloud-native equivalent). For customers that prefer a delegated subdomain (e.g., redwood.internal.acme.com -> customer-managed zone), we recommend a short CNAME pattern for service endpoints so TLS cert ownership is clear.

2) CA choice: if you run an internal CA and have client trust already provisioned across on-prem systems, using your CA for server certs gives the most control and avoids OCSP dependencies. If you cannot guarantee trust distribution, Redwood's cert-broker can issue certs signed by a customer-managed intermediate (we do not retain private keys). This hybrid lets Redwood automate rotation while keeping PKI ownership with you.

3) SAN vs wildcard: wildcards are convenient but complicate mTLS and client-cert-based routing when multiple services share ingress IPs. Prefer per-service SANs for multi-tenant clusters and a limited wildcard only for well-known front doors.

4) TLS termination: recommend terminating TLS at the cluster edge (LB) when you want consistent TLS offload and observability. For zero-trust scenarios, terminate in the sidecar/Envoy for mutual TLS to the backend. We'll sketch both flows in the workshop.

Related reading: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cCertPlaybook

On the day we'll need a list of clients that cannot reach OCSP for >24 hours (air-gapped) so we can propose short-lived certs with local caching.

Adding operational checklist items from CertOps perspective:

- Rotation cadence: 60–90 days for public-facing private endpoints; consider 30–45 days for internal services that lack OCSP reachability.
- Revocation: prefer short-lived certs over CRL reliance in air-gapped contexts; maintain an emergency revoke + issue runbook.
- Ingress patterns: 
  * LB termination: simpler, central cert management, watch out for X-Forwarded-Proto and client IP preservation.
  * Sidecar termination: per-pod certs, better mTLS posture, higher complexity.

Attachment: cert-rotation-playbook.pdf (application/pdf, 180KB)

I'll bring a sample ingress manifest and a short script we use to generate CSRs with SAN lists.

—Marissa Cole
